answer: Each agent identity must periodically solve a unique computational puzzle bound to its own key, a whisper of work no one else can reuse. A hollow shell account with no compute behind it cannot pass, while a real operator pays only a small predictable cost, like stamping copper coins one at a time. Forging ten thousand identities means buying ten thousand puzzles' worth of compute, so a sybil flood costs more than any reward it could steal.
